requests.purpose: The conserved recognizable fly body and measured jointed leg slices perform qualitative locomotion across source-bound comparison conditions.
requests.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: fresh finished hero sprite atlas for a modern explanatory animated research film. Primary request: a recognizable scientifically restrained Drosophila fruit fly, sculpted in premium tactile three-dimensional editorial illustration, with russet-red compound eyes, tan ochre segmented abdomen, dark brown thorax, delicate translucent folded wings, short antennae and fine body hairs. Generic organism, no patient identity, no disease-specific appearance. True transparent alpha, no background. Make one square image organized into TWO CLEAR HORIZONTAL ZONES with generous transparent separation. TOP TWO THIRDS: one large full side-profile fly HEAD, THORAX, ABDOMEN, FOLDED WINGS and ANTENNAE as one connected finished body, facing RIGHT, with NO LEGS attached. The fly body will be assembled with six animated legs in the film. BOTTOM ONE THIRD: exactly THREE separately isolated complete jointed insect legs, arranged in three evenly spaced columns, each from hip joint to small tarsal foot, bent naturally downward with recognizable three-part segments, facing the same rightward direction. These are the foreleg, middle leg, and hind leg shapes for this same fly. All legs fully inside their separate columns and separated from the body so their sprite crops can be articulated without editing pixels. Coherent lateral perspective, warm upper-left studio key, subtle cool fill and ivory rim, layered natural amber chitin, tiny hairs, rounded real volume and refined contact details. Rich sophisticated surface finish, readable silhouette at phone size, not vector art, not a toy, not a cartoon face, no thick black outline. No text, letters, numerical labels, logo, ruler, watermarks, vial, scenery, extra flies or decorative objects. Keep all body and leg edges uncut with ample transparent margin. This is a generic conceptual research illustration, not actual study photography or a measured assay.
requests.source_limit: Generic explanatory illustration only. No actual patient, assay apparatus, trial geometry, distance measurement, fly genotype appearance, clinical treatment or observed installation is depicted.

requests.purpose: The same fly-culture vial and paired generic condition tubes stage the normal-gene versus patient-variant comparison without claiming actual apparatus.
requests.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: fresh matching supporting-prop atlas for a modern animated research film about a candidate gene and a fruit-fly functional test. Primary request: EXACTLY THREE isolated purposeful laboratory props in THREE evenly spaced columns across one wide landscape image with true transparent alpha and generous separation. LEFT COLUMN: a short clear cylindrical fly-culture vial, open at the top, a shallow amber food-medium layer at its bottom, rounded thick glass rim, no insect inside, no cap, no scale, no text. CENTER COLUMN: one small refined specimen tube with an ivory cap and a teal collar, empty transparent glass; generic conceptual normal human gene test condition, no brand or actual sequence. RIGHT COLUMN: an identical small specimen tube with an ivory cap and a coral collar, empty transparent glass; generic conceptual patient-variant test condition, no brand or actual sequence. Match premium softly sculpted scientific editorial illustration, amber chitin-compatible warm copper details, warm upper-left key light, cool fill, ivory specular rims, coherent side-on perspective, fine glass thickness and subtle material texture. All props straight upright, separate, fully visible including bottoms; each centered in its own third, no overlap, no scene, no bench, no cast person, no hands, no fly, no floating DNA helix, no medical syringe, no stickers or wording, no logo, no watermark, no axis, no measurements. These are generic explanatory props, never the actual experiment apparatus. Exact gene names and condition labels will be native film overlays. Their shared design should make the two different test conditions instantly distinguishable while preserving identical shape.

scenes.advances: A recognizable fly plants its six feet and performs a short coordinated tripod step. The living organism remains in frame beside the generic culture vial. The fly completes another supported step to establish the living test.

Three disclosed conceptual genomic candidates separate, and BRSK1 moves into the selected-clue position before living testing. The generic culture vial joins the same fly to distinguish testing from AI selection. The fly and its sff gene label connect the candidate to an experimental comparison.

BRSK1 is linked to the fly equivalent sff, retaining the same fly. The sff label is crossed out while the fly changes to a restricted qualitative gait. The six attached feet make a visibly restricted supported step.

The normal condition tube identifies the normal human gene comparison. The fly changes from restricted stepping to coordinated movement under the normal condition. The variant condition and second restricted fly reveal partial restoration.

The paired normal and patient-variant fly results remain visibly different. The BRSK1 clue is connected to qualified diagnosis evidence for the studied families. The comparison holds as the diagnosis remains explicitly likely.

The candidate gene is carried back into the two-result living test. The normal and partial restoration remain visible in paired supported flies. The comparison ends with a likely diagnosis and explicit clinical treatment limit.

captions.text: An AI clue still needed a living test.
In Houston, Texas Children's and Baylor researchers found a promising gene change
after standard analysis of a parent and child came up empty.
Flies missing its equivalent gene had trouble moving.
A normal human gene largely restored movement.
Patient variants restored only part of it.
That comparison supports a likely diagnosis for these families.
This is evidence about a disorder, not a treatment.
